name: Fugazi
label: Dischord
lede: Fugazi kept the door at five dollars across more than a thousand shows, and when the man who once offered the Rolling Stones their own label came backstage, they politely stayed on Dischord.

eras.title: A word from a war book
eras.text: After Minor Threat and Embrace, Ian MacKaye wanted a band built around the music, not the machinery of being a band. Assembling it took a year: a bass player off Beefeater's road crew, one drummer traded for another, and a Rites of Spring singer who started out with no guitar at all.

years.h: MacKaye finds his bassist hauling gear for Beefeater
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] was on [[Beefeater|8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9]]'s road crew when MacKaye found out he played bass. [[Colin Sears|c9bbc03c-06bf-4c37-9f54-e95b51aede4c]] of [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] comes in on drums.
years.xp: MacKaye took the name from Nam, Mark Baker's oral history of American soldiers in Vietnam. The word means fake, false, not what it claims to be; Wikipedia also records the grunt backronym behind it: Fucked Up, Got Ambushed, Zipped In, as in a body bag.

years.h: Brendan Canty takes the drum stool from Sears
years.p: Sears goes back to [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]]. [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]], late of [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]], takes over.

years.src: Vice · Fugazi Live Series: Wilson Center
years.h: A $5 benefit at the Wilson Center is Fugazi's first show
years.p: They share the bill with [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition and Fire Party to raise money for Dischord's State of the Union comp. About 300 people see them as a trio, with Waiting Room already in the set.
years.xp:
The flyer drew [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] as a waiter serving the other three, which is more or less what happened next: he joined soon after. It's one of the only times the band played as a three-piece, and one of the few nights they weren't the headliner.

Joey Picuri taped the set. He kept taping for years, and this cassette became FLS0001, entry number one in the Fugazi Live Series.

yt: Full set at d.c. space, December 28, 1987
years.h: Picciotto joins as a second voice and leaves the guitar at home
years.p: Picciotto, still in [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]], starts on backing vocals, a role Wikipedia says he modeled on hip-hop production. He doesn't play guitar on a Fugazi record until Repeater.

eras.title: Free tapes and a scrapped album
eras.text: Fugazi toured like it was a job: a first US run in January 1988, then Europe. They recorded at Don Zientara's Inner Ear in Arlington, handed out demo cassettes for free, and threw away their first album when it came back sounding tired.

yt: Waiting Room, live at the Wilson Center, 1988
years.h: MacKaye plays every guitar note on the Fugazi EP
years.p: Dischord No. 30, cut at Inner Ear in June with [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]]. Picciotto only sings, and Waiting Room drops into dead silence 22 seconds in.
years.xp: The cover photo was shot at Maxwell's in Hoboken on June 30, 1988. A fan at that Maxwell's show told NPR that someone asked if they could dance to this part, and MacKaye's answer rose to a scream: "Why don't you listen for JUST! ONE! SECOOOOOOOOOOND!"

years.h: At the Wilson Center, MacKaye takes on gay-bashing
years.p: About 1,000 people pack the Wilson Center in D.C. Between songs, MacKaye talks about anti-gay attacks he'd read about in The Washington Post.

years.h: Margin Walker is what's left of a debut album the band heard as tired
years.p: Recorded in December 1988 at Southern Studios in London with Crass engineer [[John Loder|39baeee6-dc33-470e-a62d-099c89463590]], straight off an exhausting European tour, it comes out as six songs, Dischord No. 35.

years.h: Repeater gets made in the mornings
years.p: Niceley was splitting his time with culinary school, so the Inner Ear sessions ran from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

years.h: 13 Songs puts both EPs on one CD
years.p: Dischord No. 36 pairs the seven-song Fugazi EP with Margin Walker. Two records, one disc, one Dischord price.

eras.title: Everyone wants in. Nobody gets in.
eras.text: Two guitars now, 250 shows in fifteen months, and crowds that outgrew every room. The bigger Fugazi got, the more the industry circled, and the more the house rules (all ages, cheap doors, Dischord only) became the story.

years.h: Repeater arrives with two guitars and no chart position
years.p: Dischord No. 44 is the first full-length and the first with Picciotto on guitar opposite MacKaye. It missed the Billboard 200 and sold around 500,000 anyway, by Dischord's count.

years.cap: Fugazi and the band Urge in front of the tour vans, European tour, 1990
q: Excuse me, sir, would you please cut that crap out?
years.h: The $5 refund for slam-dancers who wouldn't stop
years.p: MacKaye's weapon was manners. A slam-dancer who kept hurting people got walked out and handed an envelope with his $5 back.
years.xp:
MacKaye said the polite address freaked people out more than yelling would have. The refund envelopes rode in the tour van.

Five dollars was the target door, and Wikipedia says the band saw anything more as price gouging their own fans. In later years promoters wouldn't go much below $10 to $15.

In Instrument, MacKaye stops a set to ask a man who's spitting at him to apologize, then to leave.

years.h: Fugazi play Lorton prison the day after Christmas
years.p: A free set for about 100 inmates at the Lorton Correctional Facility in Virginia, arranged by Positive Force, with songs nobody outside had heard yet.
years.xp:
The Live Series notes call it a literally captive audience; the inmates traded banter with the band, including requests for Average White Band.

Onstage in Malcolm X Park in 1996, MacKaye remembered guards confiscating "all of our ChapStick at the door" and the smell of burning garbage from the landfill next door, which he called "a metaphor for the way they treat the people that they put in there."

years.cap: Ian MacKaye at left and Guy Picciotto at right, Fugazi at UMass, 1991
yt: Live in front of the White House, January 12, 1991
years.h: A Gulf War protest show facing the White House
years.p: Days before Desert Storm, Fugazi play Lafayette Park for free in rain and sleet, on a stage of milk crates and plywood. The Positive Force show also raised support for D.C.'s homeless.
years.xp:
Per Dance of Days, as cited in the Live Series notes, organizers worried about electrocution in the rain; MacKaye decided to play anyway. The Live Series logs 1,500 people, while its own notes put the crowd nearer 3,000.

Joey Picuri taped it. The set also turns up in Instrument.

years.cap: Ian MacKaye on guitar, Fugazi at UConn, 1991
years.src: Wikipedia: Steady Diet of Nothing · Wikipedia: Fugazi
years.h: Fugazi produce Steady Diet of Nothing themselves
years.p: Dischord No. 60. Niceley had become a chef, and the label has more than 160,000 advance orders six months out.
years.xp:
Four producers meant four vetoes. "It was like we were walking on eggshells, trying not to offend each other," MacKaye said, adding that democratic mixes equal bad mixes. Lally named the record, years before the Bill Hicks line people wrongly credit.

Nirvana's Nevermind came out about two months later. Picciotto: "It was like our record could have been a hobo pissing in the forest for the amount of impact it had."

years.src: Wikipedia: In on the Kill Taker
years.h: In on the Kill Taker reaches No. 153 on Billboard and No. 24 in the UK
years.p: Dischord No. 70 is Fugazi's first Billboard 200 entry, on a label that ran out of a house in Arlington.
years.xp:
Jem Cohen found the title on a scrap of writing lying on a New York street, a rant ending with people in high places being "in on the kill taker."

This was the band's second pass at the songs. The first, recorded with Steve Albini in Chicago in fall 1992, stayed in the vault until 2026.

years.big: “There was nothing he could offer us.” Guy Picciotto
q: I would never trade what we had for what Nirvana had
years.h: Ahmet Ertegun offers Fugazi the Rolling Stones deal
years.p: Backstage during three sold-out nights at New York's Roseland Ballroom, Atlantic's chief offers them their own label and, per Wikipedia, more than $10 million to sign. They stay on Dischord.
years.xp:
Ertegun, as Paul Brannigan tells it in Louder, opened with history: "Last time I did this was when I offered The Rolling Stones their own record label and $10 million." Earlier, MacKaye had joked to an Atlantic rep that the price was $5 million guaranteed plus total creative control, then bumped it to $10 million.

"Control was what we most dearly valued," MacKaye said. Picciotto called signing "the most stupid and self-destructive thing we could possibly have done." Lollapalooza wanted them to headline that summer too; they thought about it and passed.

years.h: "Brendan #1" live in Washington DC, August 7, 1993

eras.title: Taking the engine apart
eras.text: Instead of making Kill Taker again, Fugazi pulled their sound to pieces: a boombox intro, a clarinet, a drum machine buried under two kits. Meanwhile Jem Cohen was cutting a decade of footage of them into a film.

years.cap: Ian MacKaye and Joe Lally, Fugazi at the Masquerade, Atlanta, March 29, 1996
years.h: Red Medicine comes out of months of jamming in a Connecticut house
years.p: Dischord No. 90, written in Guilford. It opens on a boombox recording and puts a clarinet on Version; the tour that followed ran 172 dates.

years.src: Louder: Why you still · Wikipedia: Fugazi
years.h: The bootleg that said “This Is Not A Fugazi T-Shirt”
years.p: A Boston company printed it. MacKaye tracked the bootlegger down and cut a deal: the money goes to charity.
years.xp:
MacKaye's pitch, per Louder: "Okay, you're funny and you're creative, so let's see how creative you are with accounting." The profits went to Rosie's Place, a Boston shelter for homeless women, for years, until the bootlegger got out of the business.

The band never sold an official shirt. "Once you're an object of investment," MacKaye said, "people will do everything they can to maximise their returns." Wikipedia gives the plainer reason too: merch means an extra person to house and feed on every tour.

years.h: Fans read the title End Hits as a goodbye
years.p: Dischord No. 110, seven months at Inner Ear. The title names the stray drum hits Canty plays after the last song, F/D.

years.h: Roadie Jerry Busher becomes Fugazi's second drummer
years.p: The End Hits drums were built from overdubs, so former roadie [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] joins Canty on a second kit to play them live. By 2002 he's on trumpet too.

yt: Fugazi and Jem Cohen discuss Instrument
years.h: Jem Cohen cuts Fugazi's decade into Instrument
years.p: A friend of MacKaye's since high school, Cohen cuts Super 8, 16mm and video from 1987 to 1998 into 115 minutes, with nearly as much time on the fans as on the band.
years.xp:
Among its scenes: Picciotto in a Philadelphia college gym in 1988, stuffing himself through a basketball hoop and performing upside down by his legs; an eighth-grade girl interviewing Picciotto and MacKaye for public-access cable; the band at Lorton prison; Canty explaining that his sister's boyfriend thought they lived on rice with no heat.

The Instrument Soundtrack, Dischord No. 120, came out alongside it, mostly instrumentals and unreleased demos.

eras.title: The best album, then the door
eras.text: Fifteen years in, Fugazi made the record a lot of fans rank first, then barely toured it. Family and other projects were pulling at all four, and the last run of shows ended in London without anyone calling it the end.

years.h: Lightning at Fort Reno, mid-Turnover
years.p: A fan told NPR that at a summer show in D.C.'s Fort Reno Park, lightning struck close by during Turnover.

years.h: The Argument brings in players from outside the band
years.p: Dischord No. 130 adds Busher, [[Kathi Wilcox|4a0dd24b-bd17-44e0-bb0c-90238a71c720]] of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]], Bridget Cross of [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]] and Amy Domingues on cello. Spin called it their best, almost fifteen years in.
years.xp:
The songs were built like Lego: each member brought riffs, the band rearranged them, tore some down into new songs and finished others in the studio. Recording ran January to April 2001 at Inner Ear and Dischord House, with the Furniture + 2 EP out alongside.

The cover crops Lady Liberty's arms from the bronze relief on Chicago's Heald Square Monument. Inside is the memorial plaque for Sandra Lee Scheuer, one of the four students killed at Kent State on May 4, 1970.

years.h: Fugazi play just 32 shows in two years
years.p: The band that once played 250 shows in fifteen months now books around family and other projects.

years.src: Fugazi Live Series: London · Dischord: Fugazi
years.h: The last night at the London Forum ends on Glueman
years.p: It's the third of three sold-out nights, an hour and 40 minutes with two encores. Nobody announced it as the final show.
years.xp:
Buff Medways and Winnebago Deal opened. Busher played trumpet and extra percussion, Picciotto droned on a guitar tuner, and both he and MacKaye stopped to deal with the crowd. The set covered every album. Nick Pellicciotto recorded it.

There was never a breakup statement. Dischord's word is an indefinite hiatus, dated 2003.

eras.title: Not broken up, just not playing
eras.text: No reunion tour, no festival payday. Fugazi opened the vault instead, pricing nearly every show they ever played the way they used to price the door, while the four of them kept playing in other bands, often with each other.

years.h: Reunion money won't do it, MacKaye says
years.p: Fugazi have been offered "an insane amount of money" to reunite, MacKaye says. The only reason to play again would be wanting to.
years.xp:
"It's not going to be money that brings us back together," he told the Washingtonian; they'd play only if they wanted to and time allowed it. Lally was living in Rome by then.

In 2019 Lally said they'd need a long stretch together first, not a rehearsal of old songs for a payday. MacKaye said in 2017 that the band never broke up, and that the four have played together privately during the hiatus.

years.src: NPR: Steady Diet · Washingtonian · Wikipedia: Fugazi Live Series · NPR: Full Disclosure
years.h: Every Fugazi live tape goes online at $5 suggested
years.p: Dischord puts Fugazi's live tapes online on a $1-to-$100 sliding scale. MacKaye dated the unlabeled ones by the accents in the crowd.
years.xp:
Most came from Joey Picuri, a friend who started taping at the first show "just out of habit," MacKaye told NPR. On the detective work: "I'd listen to the accent of someone in the crowd and go, 'Okay, that was in Italy.'"

Nothing was cleaned up; "You get what you get," said Picciotto. Wikipedia counts about 1,048 shows documented and 898 recordings up by 2025. One famous hole: Club O in Perth, November 11, 1993, where someone stole the DAT off the soundboard.

years.h: The 1988 giveaway tape goes on sale as First Demo
years.p: In January 1988 the band cut eleven songs at Inner Ear and gave ten away on cassette at shows. Dischord issues the whole session as No. 181, Turn Off Your Guns included.

years.h: Canty and Lally start [[The Messthetics|62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e]]
years.p: An instrumental trio with guitarist Anthony Pirog: the Fugazi rhythm section, back in one room.

years.h: MacKaye and Lally start [[Coriky|d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58]] with [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]]
years.p: Farina, MacKaye's partner in [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]], plays drums. The debut album was due in March and slipped to June as the pandemic shut independent record stores.

years.h: Fugazi's first and last shows hit streaming
years.p: The Live Series moves onto Bandcamp and streaming services, opening with the Wilson Center in 1987 and the London Forum in 2002.

years.src: Dischord: Albini · Wikipedia: In on the Kill Taker · NPR: Steve Albini
years.h: Fugazi release the Kill Taker they shelved in 1992
years.p: Albini Sessions was recorded with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] in Chicago in fall 1992, scrapped with his blessing, then bootlegged for decades. It comes out as a name-your-price benefit for Letters Charity.
years.xp:
The band had taken Albini up on a standing offer of free recording, at first planning an EP of songs they'd carried for years. After the rough mixes they redid all twelve at Inner Ear with Zientara and Niceley, better rehearsed the second time.

Albini died of a heart attack in May 2024, at 61. Dischord says Letters Charity was central to his life.
